extracted.intended_audience: Hospitals, health systems, and other organizations participating in or applying to be CJR-X model participants (CMS model stakeholders, data custodians, and compliance officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory proposed-rule guidance describing data sharing, privacy/security, timing, APM options, and reporting requirements for entities participating in the CJR-X CMS model. Focuses on what data are provided, how/when, and conditions for access and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and Raw Beneficiary-Identifiable Claims Data Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to make beneficiary-identifiable claims data for episodes in CJR-X available in two formats for baseline and ongoing monthly reporting: (1) summary beneficiary-identifiable claims data, which "summarizes the claims data by combining and categorizing claims data to provide a broad view of the CJR-X participant's health care expenditures and utilization" (for example, total episode spending across all of a participant's episodes); and (2) raw beneficiary-identifiable claims data, which is "unrefined and has not been grouped or combined and includes the specific claims fields... at the episode level" (for example, diagnosis codes associated with a readmission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary data is intended for participants who prefer aggregated views; raw data for those needing episode-level detail including episode summaries, excluded episode indicators, diagnosis and procedure codes, and enrollment/dual eligibility information. Both formats are intended to support monitoring, care coordination, quality improvement, and targeting interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Data Request and Data Sharing Agreement Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X participants wishing to receive summary or raw beneficiary-identifiable claims data must submit a formal data request and enter into a CJR-X data sharing agreement with CMS (submitted in a form and by a date specified by CMS). The request must indicate whether the participant wants summary data, raw data, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes that CJR-X participants must submit this signed data sharing agreement at least annually. The requirement helps ensure CMS has up-to-date information (including designated data custodians) and provides assurances that participants will appropriately protect beneficiary-identifiable data before retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestations Required When Requesting Beneficiary-Identifiable Data
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of retrieving beneficiary-identifiable claims data, the CJR-X participant must attest that: (1) it is requesting claims data of CJR-X beneficiaries who would be in an episode during the baseline period or performance year as a HIPAA covered entity; (2) the request reflects the minimum data necessary for conducting health care operations that fall within the first or second paragraph of the definition of health care operations at 45 CFR 164.501; and (3) the participant's use of claims data will be limited to developing processes and engaging in appropriate activities related to coordinating care and improving quality and efficiency and conducting population-based activities applied uniformly to all CJR-X beneficiaries, and that these data will not be used to reduce, limit or restrict care for specific Medicare beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attestations implement HIPAA minimum necessary principles and limit acceptable uses to quality/coordination/population-level activities rather than individualized denial or restriction of care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Necessary Data Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X participants must limit beneficiary-identifiable data requests to the minimum necessary for permitted uses. The proposed minimum necessary Medicare Parts A and B data elements may include but are not limited to: Medicare beneficiary identifier (ID); procedure code; sex; diagnosis code; claim ID; the from and through dates of service; the provider or supplier ID; the claim payment type; date of birth and death, if applicable; tax identification number; national provider identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS seeks comment on this list as the minimum necessary beneficiary-identifiable information for permitted health care operations under the model (proposed §512.665(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Packaging, Delivery Method, and Exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary and raw beneficiary-identifiable data would be packaged and sent to a data portal (access by request/grant) in a "flat" or binary format for retrieval by the CJR-X participant. CMS would exclude information subject to confidentiality regulations for substance use disorder patient records (42 CFR part 2) from data shared with participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must request and be granted access to the portal. The data packaging/format is intended to facilitate analytic use; specific technical formats and portal access procedures will be specified by CMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Aggregate Data Provision and De-identification Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to provide regional aggregate expenditure data (for the U.S. Census Division where the CJR-X participant is located) on total expenditures during anchor hospitalization/anchor procedure and the 90-day post-discharge period for Medicare FFS beneficiaries who would have initiated a CJR-X episode. The regional aggregate data would be de-identified in accordance with HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR 164.514(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional aggregate data would be similar in format to summary beneficiary-identifiable claims data but not beneficiary-identifiable, would comply with CMS cell suppression policy (no cell values 1–10 reported directly), and would not require a data request or be subject to the CJR-X data sharing agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline Period Data Duration and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to make 3 years of baseline period data available to CJR-X participants who enter into a data sharing agreement, for beneficiaries who would have been included in an episode during the baseline period. The 3-year baseline is to match the baseline used to create participants' target prices and would roll forward one year every performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS would provide these 3 years of baseline data upon request prior to the start of each performance year (proposed at least 1 month prior). CMS considered 1 or 4 years but proposes 3 years as sufficient for identifying cost drivers and practice patterns used in target price construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Year Data Frequency and Claims Run-Out Period
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to make updated raw and summary beneficiary-identifiable claims data and regional aggregate data available to CJR-X participants as frequently as monthly during a performance year, upon request and execution of a data sharing agreement, and to continue sharing claims data for up to 6 months beyond the end of that performance year to capture claims run out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly updates are chosen to align with the 90-day post-discharge episode window and to enable timely identification of potential beneficiaries and care improvement opportunities. The 6-month run-out reflects internal findings that most Medicare claims are final within 6 months and aligns with reconciliation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X Data Sharing Agreement Content and Safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: The CJR-X data sharing agreement is proposed to include terms requiring: (1) compliance with HIPAA Privacy Rule use/disclosure requirements and the CJR-X requirements; (2) additional privacy, security, and breach-notification requirements specified by CMS; (3) contractual binding of downstream recipients/business associates to the same terms and conditions; (4) identification of designated data custodian(s) responsible for compliance and incident notification; and (5) requirements related to administrative, physical, and technical safeguards, limitations on further use/disclosure, procedures for responding to data incidents/breaches, and data destruction/retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes similar agreements exist in other models and Medicare Shared Savings Program; provisions will be in addition to legal requirements (HIPAA Privacy, Security, and Breach Notification Rules at 45 CFR parts 160 and 164) and would not prohibit disclosures otherwise required by law. CMS seeks comment on additional privacy, security, breach notification, and other requirements to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding Downstream Recipients and Business Associates
rubrics_metrics.description: The data sharing agreement would require the CJR-X participant to contractually bind each downstream recipient of the beneficiary-identifiable data that is a business associate or performs similar functions to the same terms and conditions to which the CJR-X participant is bound, as a condition of the downstream recipient receiving the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that contractors, analytics vendors, and other business associates handling beneficiary-identifiable data must meet the same privacy/security/usage constraints as the CJR-X participant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Further Disclosure and Permissible Recipients (Considered Prohibitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is considering prohibiting further disclosure of beneficiary-identifiable data, not otherwise required by law, to anyone who is not a 'HIPAA covered entity or business associate' or to an individual practitioner in a treatment relationship with the CJR-X beneficiary (or that practitioner's business associates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS solicits comment on what disclosures might be appropriate to permit or prohibit; recognizes some participants may need business associates (e.g., contractors for analytics) or treatment providers to accomplish CJR-X goals under applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions, Remedial Actions, and Termination of Data Access for Misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CJR-X participant misuses or discloses beneficiary-identifiable data in violation of statutory or regulatory requirements or the data sharing agreement, CMS proposes that the participant would no longer be eligible to retrieve beneficiary-identifiable data and may be subject to additional sanctions and penalties available under law. CMS may discontinue provision of data sharing and reports to the model participant upon determination that grounds for remedial action have taken place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data sharing agreement would include terms to enforce these consequences and CMS requests comment on this enforcement approach (proposed §512.665(e)(1)(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: APM Eligibility Criteria and Two APM Options (AAPM and non-AAPM)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered an Advanced APM (per 42 CFR 414.1415), an APM must: require use of Certified Electronic Health Record Technology (CEHRT); be subject to payment based on quality measures; and require entities to bear financial risk. CMS proposes two APM options for CJR-X: an AAPM option for participants who attest to meeting the CEHRT requirement, and a non-AAPM option for participants who do not meet CEHRT (who may still be considered an APM entity in a MIPS APM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting/attesting to CEHRT is voluntary; participants who attest would be required to retain and provide attestation and EHR certification IDs to CMS on an annual basis. The choice affects clinicians' potential Qualifying APM Participant (QP) determinations and MIPS APM/APP reporting, but does not otherwise change model requirements/opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: APM CEHRT Attestation and Documentation Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X participants who wish to participate in the AAPM option must attest annually, prior to the start of each performance year, that they meet the CEHRT use requirement (per 42 CFR 414.1305), and must retain and provide CMS access to the attestation and provide their CMS EHR Certification IDs on an annual basis prior to the end of each performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attestation is required in a form and manner and by dates specified by CMS; failure to attest results in assignment to the non-AAPM option and may affect clinicians' QP determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Arrangements List and Clinician Engagement Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each CJR-X participant is required to submit information about eligible clinicians or MIPS eligible clinicians who enter into financial arrangements with the CJR-X participant to support cost/quality goals. CMS proposes defining the 'financial arrangements list' as the list of eligible clinicians or MIPS eligible clinicians with a financial arrangement with the CJR-X participant, collaborator, collaboration agent, or downstream collaboration agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The financial arrangements list must be submitted in a form and manner and by the date specified by CMS on a quarterly basis during each performance year (or attest there are no individuals to report). CMS will use the list to make QP determinations and for APP reporting/scoring. Participants must retain and provide CMS access to the list upon request.
